description: Olivine waitlists reads whose requested version is ahead of current_version, but batch application wakes only the exact batch-end version. A waiter for an intermediate version remains stranded after current_version advances past it. On develop, the waitlist deadline returned by WaitingList.insert is also ignored; the expiration behavior from main commit 81ef5213 / PR #73 is absent. Repo point reads call their TransactionBuilder with infinity and retry retryable storage failures without an end-to-end deadline, so a stranded or unavailable read appears to hang forever. Implement via TDD: wake every waiter at or below the applied version while preserving future waiters; schedule and expire idle waiters with a terminal timeout; add a configurable default 5-second transaction deadline measured once with monotonic time and preserved across retries/nested work, bounding calls and retry sleeps by remaining time; terminate the active builder cleanly and surface a clear timeout with the last retry reason. Preserve the current Demux streaming and ingestion backpressure behavior.

comments.text: TDD evidence: RED reproduced (1) an intermediate-version waiter left queued after a batch advanced beyond it, (2) an idle waitlisted read that never received a terminal reply, (3) retry loops that outlived their configured transaction timeout, (4) nested work that reset the timeout, and (5) a point read blocked forever on an unresponsive TransactionBuilder. GREEN: 71 focused tests; 734 subsystem tests plus 65 properties; full suite 2,541 tests, 158 properties, 13 doctests; format, Credo strict, and Dialyzer all pass. Design: Olivine wakes every waiter at or below the applied version and independently expires parked reads; Repo measures one monotonic deadline per outer transaction and caps layout fetches, builder calls, range batches, commits, and retry sleeps without changing Demux ordering or backpressure.

title: Bound post-recovery reads and wake every readable Olivine waiter
